XI.}}|{{sc|according to s. iohn.}}|251}}</noinclude>goe{{ls}}t thou thither againe? {{verse|chapter=11|verse=9}} {{sc|Iesvs}} an{{ls}}vvered, Are there not tvvelue houres of the day? If a man vvalke in the day, he {{ls}}tumbleth not: becau{{ls}}e he {{ls}}eeth the light of this world: {{verse|chapter=11|verse=10}} but if he walke in the night, he {{ls}}tumbleth, becau{{ls}}e the light is not in him. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=11}} The{{ls}}e things he {{ls}}aid: and after this he {{ls}}aith to them, Lazarus our frende {{ls}}leepeth: but I goe that I may rai{{ls}}e him from {{ls}}leepe. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=12}} His Di{{ls}}ciples therfore {{ls}}aid, Lord, if he {{ls}}leepe, he {{ls}}hal be {{ls}}afe. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=13}} but {{sc|Iesvs}} {{ls}}pake of his death: & they thought that he {{ls}}pake c {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''de dormitione {{ls}}omni''.}}∷ of the {{ls}}leeping of {{ls}}leepe. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=14}} Then therfore {{sc|Iesvs}} {{ls}}aid to them plainely, Lazarus is dead: {{verse|chapter=11|verse=15}} and I am glad for your {{ls}}ake, that you may beleeue, becau{{ls}}e I vvas not there. but let vs goe to him. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=16}} Thomas therfore, vvho is called Didymus, {{ls}}aid to his condi{{ls}}ciples, Let vs al{{ls}}o goe, to die vvith him.

{{verse|chapter=11|verse=17}} {{sc|Iesvs}} therfore came, and found him novv hauing been foure daies in the graue. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=18}} (and Bethánia vvas nigh to Hieru{{ls}}alem about fiftene furlonges.) {{verse|chapter=11|verse=19}} And many of the Ievves vvere come to Martha and Marie, to comfort them concerning theire brother. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=20}} Martha therfore vvhen {{ls}}he heard that {{sc|Iesvs}} vvas come, vvent to meete him: but Marie {{ls}}at at home. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=21}} {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Go{{ls}}pel in a Ma{{ls}}{{ls}}e for the dead vpon the day of the burial or depo{{ls}}ition.}}Martha therfore {{ls}}aid to {{sc|Iesvs}}, Lord if thou had{{ls}}t been here, my brother had not died. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=22}} but novv al{{ls}}o I knovv that vvhat things {{ls}}oeuer thou {{ls}}halt a{{ls}}ke of God, God vvil giue thee. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=23}} {{sc|Iesvs}} {{ls}}aith to her, Thy brother {{ls}}hal ri{{ls}}e againe. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=24}} Martha {{ls}}aith to him, I knovv that he {{ls}}hal ri{{ls}}e againe in the re{{ls}}urrection, in the la{{ls}}t day. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=25}} {{sc|Iesvs}} {{ls}}aid to her, I am the re{{ls}}urrection and the life: he that beleeueth in me, although he be dead, {{ls}}hal liue. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=26}} and euery one that liueth, and beleeueth in me, {{ls}}hal not die for euer, Beleeue{{ls}}t thou this? {{verse|chapter=11|verse=27}} She {{ls}}aith to him, Yea Lord, I haue beleeued that thou art {{sc|Christ}} the {{ls}}onne of God that art come into this vvorld.⊣

{{verse|chapter=11|verse=28}} And vvhen {{ls}}he had {{ls}}aid the{{ls}}e things, {{ls}}he vvent, and called Marie her {{ls}}i{{ls}}ter {{ls}}ecretely, {{ls}}aying, The mai{{ls}}ter is come, & calleth thee. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=29}} She, when {{ls}}he heard, ri{{ls}}eth quickely, & commeth to him. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=30}} For {{sc|Iesvs}} was not yet come into the towne: but he vvas yet in that place vvhere Martha had mette him. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=31}} The Ievves therfore that vvere vvith her in the hou{{ls}}e and did comfort her, vvhen they {{ls}}avv Marie that {{ls}}he ro{{ls}}e quickly and vvent forth, folovved her, {{ls}}aying, That {{ls}}he goeth to the graue, to vveepe there. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=32}} Marie therfore vvhen<noinclude>{{continues|{{ls}}he}}</noinclude>
